reviews.title: Fantastic App
reviews.text: This app is exactly what I was looking for. It allows you to learn in context all in one spot. I love that you get real people narrating the texts almost of the time as well and that you can make your own lessons out of the videos, podcasts, books, and websites you want to watch or read. I actually use it to understand websites I am looking at. The only thing I would love to see eventually is in the vocabulary review section I would love to see more interactive activities. I want to have to type or speak, not just choose the right answer. I would also love there to be a pronunciation section where you can either record and compare the pronunciation or it simply tells you how close you are. Something that this app has is that it is almost a one stop shop. With these changes I think it will be this for sure.

reviews.title: Stuck in English
reviews.text: I signed up for the application trial with the goal of reviewing French and improving my listening comprehension skills. The app however had gotten stuck with two target languages: English and French. As a result, I was getting daily email reminders telling me how I can become better at English, in English. I was getting notifications about studying English. No notifications nor emails about French. There is a way in the app’s settings to remove a language, but English would somehow get added back the next day. I just couldn’t bring myself to pay $120 per year to get daily reminders about learning English so I canceled my trial. It’s really too bad because what I saw for learning French looked pretty great.

reviews.title: Great app for language learning
reviews.text: Great app to learn a new language.  You can import YouTube videos, documents, certain books(depending on copyright), Podcasts etc. You can then study the content and highlight words and phrases.  Highlighting a phrase is called a LingQ and it really is the best way to learn because individual words may have a different meaning alone but with other words mean something completely different.   I didn’t give it 5 stars because there are a few things that they need to improve/fix. One thing that is annoying is when you import something it will sometimes split a complete sentence.  So if you’re studying in “view sentence” mode then half of that sentence is on one page and the other half is on the next.  Or you may even have half of the last sentence, the beginning of the next sentence and then the end of that sentence afterwards and so on.  This is a problem when studying because depending on where it splits can sometimes change the meaning of the sentence.  If the app knows where the sentence starts and ends, then it should be able to fix this issue.  I know you can manually do it but it is very tedious and takes a lot of time to do.  Most of the LingQ lessons are perfect and don’t do that, only importing from what I can see.  Other than that, the app works great and they are consistently pushing out updates to improve it weekly.

reviews.title: Excellent AI integration and powerful import tools
reviews.text:
LingQ is in a new golden age. I am really impressed with its AI integration, and the development of its import tools over the years. I don’t think any other apps come close and I highly recommend it.

I’ve been using this on and off since probably 2019 and over the years. Early on, the app was kind of clunky and the community definitions were sometimes subpar or (at least for Chinese) have too much info.

When I got the lifetime license later on in 2021, I remember having to type the URL manually to get the page that sold it. The renewal pages leading up to it felt overly pushy and a bit sketchy—to be frank. I hope that’s improved.

The import function is really powerful for YouTube, Netflix, and anything else. I like the Language Reactor extension but LingQ already has something similar built right in. Amazing. 

No need to mess with the advanced tutorials Refold shows with Anki integrations. LingQ has none of that effort and is an all-in-one tool.

LingQ’s AI integration (called Lynx AI) has been really good at what I’ve used it for which is to simplify down imported lessons, create definitions, and ask questions about existing lessons. I think it would benefit from a more powerful model in the future though.

reviews.title: LingQ Impressions
reviews.text: The LingQ concept is great, although the implementation is somewhat rough at best. The AI quality ranges from very poor to almost okay. Translations can range from being completely off base and marginally correct to good. The AI pronunciation is not infrequently absolutely terrible, and sometimes inaudible. I keep using it because it is the only software package of its kind and despite the shortcomings, I am learning a lot. Please work on making the software as amazingly fantastic as it can be.

I pay for a yearly subscription to LingQ and appreciate it more and more, the more I use it.   It goes without saying that I am a huge fan of polyglot Steve Kaufman.

reviews.title: LingQ to learn Ukrainian…Just start here…with LingQ!
reviews.text:
I should have started using LingQ from the start of my Ukrainian studies. I always find using LingQ to be a better learning tool than every other app; sounding out words as I am reading them is a necessary step to fluency, since I am a visual learner.

Slow beginnings are just “a click away” as you find yourself learning step by step, while being supported by built-in LingQ’s robust language integration. 

Simple page and specific lesson oriented vocabulary review tools, not found anywhere else help you focus on the content you see and hear. 

Other game type apps are ok for picture to word vocabulary learning, but LingQ puts it all together.

So much thought has been put into the creation of LingQ, that I keep coming back to it day after day!

reviews.title: There’s nothing better, but it needs real improvements
reviews.text: There is no better app for reading ebooks and listening to podcast audio in a foreign language. The interface for tapping one or more words then fetching a word’s transcription, for both its dictionary definition and both in-context definition, and saving it, is unparalleled. But why does it take so long to load? Why is the app’s upload interface so glitchy compared to the one on the Web? Why can’t it auto-scroll in the same interface with the click-to-translate? Why doesn’t it make an attempt to count or save word stems? I really wish this app were just a little better.
